assessments.reasoning: Authenticity follows from publisher_live at creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt. Integrity follows from the matching reported digest for [5884,6024) and the complete-file digest shared with publisher_pin. Relevance follows from section 4(a) naming both rights and their holder. Interpretation follows from its express coverage of waiver and licensing, ending with “otherwise affected by this document.” Applicability follows from the Statement of Purpose identifying the Affirmer as the person applying CC0 to a Work to the extent of their ownership. The contradiction check against sections 1(iv), 2, 3 and 4(c) confirms the exclusion under both mechanisms and preserves the distinction between the Affirmer and other holders.

challenge.method: Tested the broad language of section 2 and the conditional license and residual non-assertion in section 3 separately against section 4(a). Checked the holder limitation against the Statement of Purpose and section 4(c).
challenge.results: Section 2 waives the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the extent permitted by law. Section 4(a) expressly excludes the Affirmer's patents and trademarks from that waiver. If the waiver is judged ineffective, section 3 licenses only the Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights to the affected extent. Its residual undertaking has the same subject, and section 4(a) expressly excludes licensing the specified rights. Section 1(iv) likewise subjects unfair-competition rights to 4(a). Other holders' rights receive separate treatment in 4(c).

limitations: The finding concerns the stated effect of applying this instrument. Separate grants, defenses and ownership of particular rights require separate evidence.
Section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for obtaining third-party clearances. It gives no assurance that a proposed use is clear of other people's rights.
reasoning: Section 4(a) expressly excludes trademark and patent rights “held by Affirmer” from waiver, surrender, licensing and any other effect of this document. That language covers both routes by which CC0 makes copyright and related rights available.
